content.value_statement: Accessibility issues block users and create release risk when teams rely only on automated scores. This skill guides WCAG 2.2 audits with practical checks, accessible patterns, and prioritized remediation.
actual_capabilities: Review UI code and page behavior against WCAG 2.2 POUR principles.
Identify missing alt text, labels, landmarks, focus states, and keyboard paths.
Suggest accessible HTML, CSS, ARIA, and live region patterns.
Guide manual tests for keyboard navigation, screen readers, zoom, contrast, and reduced motion.
Reference common WCAG 2.2 changes and severity priorities.
limitations: Does not replace legal accessibility certification.
Cannot verify real assistive technology behavior without manual testing on target devices.
Automated tools may miss semantic, cognitive, and workflow issues.
Requires access to relevant page markup, styles, and interaction details.

use_cases.title: Fix Component Accessibility
use_cases.description: Find keyboard, focus, label, contrast, and ARIA issues before a component ships.

use_cases.title: Validate Inclusive Interaction Design
use_cases.description: Check flows for target size, motion, content clarity, help placement, and non-drag alternatives.

use_cases.title: Plan Release Accessibility Testing
use_cases.description: Create a test pass that combines automated scans, keyboard checks, screen reader checks, and WCAG mapping.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Quick Accessibility Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a page or component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this page or component for WCAG 2.2 issues. Focus on alt text, labels, headings, keyboard access, and color contrast. Return prioritized fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Modal or Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this modal or form flow. Identify screen reader, focus management, error handling, and keyboard issues. Suggest accessible patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Release Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an accessibility test plan for this feature. Include automated checks, manual keyboard tests, screen reader checks, and WCAG 2.2 criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Audit Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these accessibility audit results to WCAG 2.2 success criteria. Prioritize by user impact, propose fixes, and note verification steps.

output_examples.input: Audit a checkout form before release.
output: Missing labels and error descriptions are highest priority because users cannot complete required fields reliably.
Add visible labels, programmatic descriptions, and focus movement to the first invalid field.
Verify with keyboard-only navigation, screen reader announcements, and 200 percent zoom.

output_examples.input: Review a tab interface for keyboard support.
output: The tab list needs arrow key navigation, selected state updates, and clear focus visibility.
Prefer native buttons for tabs and connect each tab to its panel with accessible names.
Test Tab, Shift+Tab, Arrow keys, Enter, Space, and screen reader announcements.

output_examples.input: Turn an automated scan into a fix plan.
output: Group findings by user impact, starting with blockers for forms, navigation, and focus movement.
Map each issue to the related WCAG 2.2 criterion and define a manual verification step.
Use automated tools again after fixes, then complete manual keyboard and screen reader checks.

best_practices: Provide component markup, styles, and interaction rules with the prompt.
Ask for WCAG criterion mapping when you need traceable remediation.
Combine automated tooling with keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and contrast checks.
anti_patterns: Treating an automated score as complete compliance.
Removing focus outlines without an equal visible replacement.
Adding ARIA roles where native HTML already provides semantics.

faq.question: Does this skill run accessibility tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples. Tool execution depends on the host agent and user approval.

faq.question: Does it support WCAG 2.2?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers WCAG 2.2 principles, common success criteria, and newer 2.2 requirements.

faq.question: Can it certify legal accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. It helps find and fix issues, but legal certification needs qualified review and local legal guidance.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Provide page markup, component code, screenshots, audit results, or clear descriptions of the user flow.

faq.question: Can it help with screen reader issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests accessible names, live regions, focus management, landmarks, labels, and manual screen reader checks.

faq.question: Is it only for developers?
faq.answer: No. Designers, QA teams, content authors, and product teams can use it for accessibility planning and review.
